description: Browser camera agent — getUserMedia streams webcam to a <video>, a canvas grabs a JPEG on trigger, POSTs base64 + prompt to /api/vision, renders the multimodal LLM response as text and as an overlay on the captured frame.

defaults.headline: Point the camera, ask a question
defaults.subheadline: Capture a frame, send it to a multimodal LLM, see the answer drawn on top of the image.

archetypes: snap a photo ask an llm

gotchas: getUserMedia for camera requires HTTPS outside localhost. Behind plain HTTP on any real hostname the call fails with NotAllowedError before the permission prompt ever appears.

iOS Safari auto-rotates camera frames based on device orientation but <canvas>.drawImage does NOT. On mobile portrait the captured JPEG is sideways — you must read `(video as any).videoWidth/videoHeight` after `loadedmetadata` fires, and apply orientation if building a production app.
canvas.toDataURL('image/jpeg', quality) is synchronous and blocks the main thread on large canvases. For >1080p frames, switch to canvas.toBlob() with a callback — it's off-thread and ~3× faster.
Base64 JPEGs are ~1.33× their binary size. For high-res frames (>500KB), send as multipart/form-data or use toBlob() + binary fetch to cut the payload.

`facingMode: 'environment'` (rear camera) is a hint, not a guarantee. Desktop browsers ignore it, and some Android devices return a front camera anyway. Always offer a flip-camera button that re-calls getUserMedia with `{ video: { deviceId } }`.
The MediaStream keeps the camera LED on until every track.stop() is called. Don't just pause the <video>; call `stream.getTracks().forEach(t => t.stop())` when the user is done.
